internal.courseworkclassoption: Class option forwarding and filtering helper.

entries.name: courseworksetup
entries.description: Set course metadata and output configuration. Each call replaces the supplied values and retains the other values. Fonts load with the class. Select a font through a class option.
entries.arguments: Supply a list of keys separated by commas. Put braces around values that contain commas or LaTeX. See the setup key table.

entries.name: courseworkvalue
entries.description: Expand one of the six metadata values. This command reads metadata only. It does not read modes, page breaks, or fonts.
entries.arguments: `key` identifies `author`, `course-code`, `course-title`, `term`, `textbook`, or `textbook-author`. Each value defaults to empty.

entries.name: makecourseworktitle
entries.description: Print a title with the course title, code, author, and date. The command does not add contents or assignment headings.
entries.arguments: `title` is optional and defaults to empty. `date` defaults to the configured term. Set page breaks and page numbers explicitly in the front matter.

entries.name: makeassignmentheading
entries.description: Print an assignment heading. The left column contains the author and title. The right column contains the course title and date. The command uses an empty style for the current page.
entries.arguments: `title` is optional and defaults to empty. `date` defaults to the configured term. Set page breaks and page numbers explicitly in the front matter.

entries.name: assignment
entries.description: Start a new assignment. The command resets its declarations. Each assignment ID must be unique in the document.
entries.arguments:
`title` supplies the assignment heading. `id` is required. Start it with a letter or digit. Use letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores for subsequent characters.

`directory` is required and uses a path relative to the project root. `number` is a positive integer. It defaults to the next assignment number. `problems-title` defaults to `Problem Set`.

entries.name: declareproblem
entries.description: Declare a problem after its assignment and before assignment output. The declaration supplies a stable ID and an optional display title. It does not read fragments.
entries.arguments: `id` uses the assignment ID character rules. It must be unique within the assignment. `title` defaults to empty.

entries.name: printassignment
entries.description: Print the current assignment once. The renderer numbers selected problems from 1 in the specified order for every role. Canonical labels use `prob:<assignment-id>:<problem-id>`. Reference values include the assignment number.
entries.arguments: `problems` contains IDs separated by commas. An omitted or empty value selects all problems in declaration order. Duplicate or unknown IDs cause errors. An assignment without problems causes an error. Repeated output and missing required files also cause errors.

entries.name: priming
entries.description: Print a short priming paragraph with a bold italic label.
entries.arguments: `text` supplies the content after the label.

entries.name: procedure
entries.description: Print a short procedure paragraph with a bold italic label.
entries.arguments: `text` supplies the content after the label.

entries.name: NN
entries.description: Print the symbol for natural numbers in blackboard bold. The command works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: ZZ
entries.description: Print the symbol for integers in blackboard bold. The command works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: QQ
entries.description: Print the symbol for rational numbers in blackboard bold. The command works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: RR
entries.description: Print the symbol for real numbers in blackboard bold. The command works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: CC
entries.description: Print the symbol for complex numbers in blackboard bold. The command works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: dd
entries.description: Print an upright differential d. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments. Write the variable separately. Add any required spacing separately.

entries.name: deriv
entries.description: Print an ordinary derivative with `diffcoeff`. Use the command in math mode. The command does not consume a subsequent bracketed expression as an evaluation point.
entries.arguments: `order` defaults to 1. To form an operator, leave `expression` empty. `variable` identifies the differentiation variable.

entries.name: pderiv
entries.description: Print a partial derivative with `diffcoeff`. Use the command in math mode. The command does not consume a subsequent bracketed expression as an evaluation point.
entries.arguments: `order` defaults to 1. To form an operator, leave `expression` empty. `variable` identifies the differentiation variable.

entries.name: integral
entries.description: Print an integral with an upright differential. The command works in text and math mode. The size option changes only the integral sign. `medium` and `large` enlarge the display sign by one and two `relsize` steps, respectively. Nested calls default to `normal`.
entries.arguments: `size` defaults to `normal`. Unknown sizes cause errors. Empty `lower` and `upper` arguments omit the corresponding bounds. All four braced arguments are required.

entries.name: evalat
entries.description: Evaluate an expression at two bounds with a right evaluation bar. The command works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` supplies the expression to evaluate. `lower` and `upper` supply the endpoints. Either endpoint can be empty.

entries.name: evalbracket
entries.description: Evaluate an expression at two bounds with a left square bracket and a right evaluation bar. The command works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` supplies the expression to evaluate. `lower` and `upper` supply the endpoints. Either endpoint can be empty.

entries.name: paren
entries.description: Print paired parentheses. The form without a star uses a fixed size. The starred form selects the size automatically. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` supplies the enclosed content. For an explicit size, use an optional argument such as `\big` or `\Big` instead of the star.

entries.name: bracket
entries.description: Print paired square brackets. The form without a star uses a fixed size. The starred form selects the size automatically. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` supplies the enclosed content. For an explicit size, use an optional argument such as `\big` or `\Big` instead of the star.

entries.name: abs
entries.description: Print paired absolute-value bars. The form without a star uses a fixed size. The starred form selects the size automatically. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` supplies the enclosed content. For an explicit size, use an optional argument such as `\big` or `\Big` instead of the star.

entries.name: norm
entries.description: Print paired norm bars. The form without a star uses a fixed size. The starred form selects the size automatically. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` supplies the enclosed content. For an explicit size, use an optional argument such as `\big` or `\Big` instead of the star.

entries.name: average
entries.description: Print an average in angle brackets. The command works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` supplies the content. For covariance, supply a pair such as `X,Y` in the same argument.

entries.name: expectation
entries.description: Print expectation E with square brackets. The command works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` supplies the content. For covariance, supply a pair such as `X,Y` in the same argument.

entries.name: variance
entries.description: Print variance Var with fixed-size parentheses. The command works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` supplies the content. For covariance, supply a pair such as `X,Y` in the same argument.

entries.name: covariance
entries.description: Print covariance Cov with automatically sized parentheses. The command works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` supplies the content. For covariance, supply a pair such as `X,Y` in the same argument.

entries.name: probability
entries.description: Print probability P with automatically sized parentheses. The command works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: `expression` supplies the content. For covariance, supply a pair such as `X,Y` in the same argument.

entries.name: conditionalprob
entries.description: Print a conditional probability with an automatically sized middle bar. The command works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: `event` supplies the event expression. `condition` supplies the condition expression.

entries.name: mathbold
entries.description: Print bold mathematics in text or math mode. The command uses `bm` for legacy mathematics. With `unicode-math`, it uses the Unicode bold alphabet. Nested upright and italic alphabets retain their shape.
entries.arguments: `expression` supplies a symbol or complete mathematics expression.

entries.name: slashfrac
entries.description: Print a compact slash fraction with a raised numerator and a lowered denominator. The command works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: `numerator` and `denominator` supply mathematics expressions.

entries.name: mathtext
entries.description: Insert text between half-em spaces in math mode.
entries.arguments: `prefix` defaults to empty. If required, use punctuation such as a comma for the prefix. The command prints `text` with `\text`.

entries.name: combinations
entries.description: Print n choose k in C notation. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: `n` supplies the total count. `k` supplies the selected count.

entries.name: permutations
entries.description: Print n-permute-k in P notation. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: `n` supplies the total count. `k` supplies the selected count.

entries.name: colvector
entries.description: Print a column array in parentheses. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: `alignment` defaults to `r`. You can also use `l` or `c`. Separate rows with `\\`.

entries.name: questioneq
entries.description: Print an equals sign with a question mark above it. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: checkeq
entries.description: Print an equals sign with a check mark above it. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: crosseq
entries.description: Print an equals sign with a cross above it. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: vect
entries.description: Print a bold vector. The command works in text and math mode. It uses the active mathematics backend.
entries.arguments: `symbol` supplies the vector symbol. You can use Greek letters if the font supports them.

entries.name: uprightvect
entries.description: Print a upright bold vector. The command works in text and math mode. It uses the active mathematics backend.
entries.arguments: `symbol` supplies the vector symbol. You can use Greek letters if the font supports them.

entries.name: unitvect
entries.description: Print a bold vector with a hat. The command works in text and math mode. It uses the active mathematics backend.
entries.arguments: `symbol` supplies the vector symbol. You can use Greek letters if the font supports them.

entries.name: uprightunitvect
entries.description: Print a upright bold vector with a hat. The command works in text and math mode. It uses the active mathematics backend.
entries.arguments: `symbol` supplies the vector symbol. You can use Greek letters if the font supports them.

entries.name: xhat
entries.description: Print a x unit vector with a bold hat. The Latin letter is upright. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: yhat
entries.description: Print a y unit vector with a bold hat. The Latin letter is upright. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: zhat
entries.description: Print a z unit vector with a bold hat. The Latin letter is upright. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: rhat
entries.description: Print a r unit vector with a bold hat. The Latin letter is upright. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: shat
entries.description: Print a s unit vector with a bold hat. The Latin letter is upright. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: thetahat
entries.description: Print a theta unit vector with a bold hat. The Greek letter uses the active Greek mathematics alphabet. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: phihat
entries.description: Print a phi unit vector with a bold hat. The Greek letter uses the active Greek mathematics alphabet. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: grad
entries.description: Print a bold nabla gradient operator. The command does not consume the subsequent expression. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments. Write the function or field after the command.

entries.name: laplacian
entries.description: Print a bold squared nabla with a thin space after it. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments. Write the function or field after the command.

entries.name: separation
entries.description: Print script r for separation notation. The command uses the bundled PDF glyphs. It works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments. Both glyph PDFs must be available through kpathsea.

entries.name: separationvect
entries.description: Print bold script r for separation notation. The command uses the bundled PDF glyphs. It works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments. Both glyph PDFs must be available through kpathsea.

entries.name: separationunit
entries.description: Print bold script r with a hat for separation notation. The command uses the bundled PDF glyphs. It works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments. Both glyph PDFs must be available through kpathsea.

entries.name: volumeregion
entries.description: Print the volume domain symbol v. The legacy backend uses `txmi` glyphs. The Unicode backend uses ordinary italic letters. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: surfaceregion
entries.description: Print the surface domain symbol s. The legacy backend uses `txmi` glyphs. The Unicode backend uses ordinary italic letters. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: pathregion
entries.description: Print the path domain symbol p. The legacy backend uses `txmi` glyphs. The Unicode backend uses ordinary italic letters. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: kB
entries.description: Print the Boltzmann constant symbol. The command works in text and math mode. It prints a symbol without a numeric value.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: NA
entries.description: Print the Avogadro constant symbol. The command works in text and math mode. It prints a symbol without a numeric value.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments.

entries.name: dbar
entries.description: Print a barred differential symbol for an inexact differential. Use the command in math mode.
entries.arguments: The command has no arguments. Write the quantity after the command.

entries.name: constantvalue
entries.description: Print a rounded constant with SI units: 1.381 × 10⁻²³ J/K or 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹. These are the existing library values, not exact SI definitions. The command works in text and math mode.
entries.arguments: `name` is required. Use `boltzmann` or `avogadro`. Other names cause errors.

entries.name: theorem
entries.description: The environment shares the theorem counter. This counter resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Put a standard `\label` in the body for a reference.
entries.arguments: The title is optional. The body accepts ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: lemma
entries.description: The environment shares the theorem counter. This counter resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Put a standard `\label` in the body for a reference.
entries.arguments: The title is optional. The body accepts ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.description: The environment shares the theorem counter. This counter resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Put a standard `\label` in the body for a reference.

entries.name: algorithm
entries.description: The environment shares the theorem counter. This counter resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Put a standard `\label` in the body for a reference.
entries.arguments: The title is optional. The body accepts ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: definition
entries.description: The environment has its own counter. This counter resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Put a standard `\label` in the body for a reference.
entries.arguments: The title is optional. The body accepts ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: example
entries.description: The environment has its own counter. This counter resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Put a standard `\label` in the body for a reference.
entries.arguments: The title is optional. The body accepts ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: remark
entries.description: The environment has its own counter. This counter resets by section. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Put a standard `\label` in the body for a reference.
entries.arguments: The title is optional. The body accepts ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: summary
entries.description: The environment has its own counter. This counter resets by subsection. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument. Put a standard `\label` in the body for a reference.
entries.arguments: The title is optional. The body accepts ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: note
entries.description: The environment has no number. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument.
entries.arguments: The title is optional. The body accepts ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: caveat
entries.description: The environment has no number. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument.
entries.arguments: The title is optional. The body accepts ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: warning
entries.description: The environment has no number. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument.
entries.arguments: The title is optional. The body accepts ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: question
entries.description: The environment has no number. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument.
entries.arguments: The title is optional. The body accepts ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: speculation
entries.description: The environment has no number. The first braced word is body content, not a label argument.
entries.arguments: The title is optional. The body accepts ordinary text and mathematics.

entries.name: proof
entries.description: Print a proof with its closing marker. The environment has no number. `courseenvironments` loads this environment from `amsthm`.
entries.arguments: The optional title replaces `Proof`. If the proof ends with a display, use `\qedhere` inside the display as required.

entries.name: formula
entries.description: Print a mathematics display with a bold text tag and a separate sequential formula counter. References return the counter value independently of the displayed tag. The counter does not reset by section. The environment does not force a subsequent line break.
entries.arguments: The optional tag defaults to `Formula N`. The body is already in math mode. Put `\label` inside the environment.

entries.name: subparts
entries.description: Print a list of subparts with labels (a), (b), and subsequent letters.
entries.arguments: The environment has no arguments. Start each part with `\item`.

entries.name: mathtable
entries.description: Print a floating table with a mathematics array and an automatic top rule. Options apply only to the current table.
entries.arguments:
`columns` supplies the array alignment. `caption` and `label` default to empty. A label requires a caption. `placement` defaults to `ht!`, or `H` in notes.

Supply row endings. Supply `\bottomrule` if required.

entries.name: tableheading
entries.description: Print a centered text heading on two lines for a mathematics table column.
entries.arguments: `top` and `bottom` supply text. Put dollar signs around any mathematics.

entries.name: courseenvironmentsetup
entries.description: Set global defaults for subsequent mathematics tables. Notes select `H` and `-2ex`. Other contexts default to `ht!` and `-1em`.
entries.arguments: `table-placement` supplies the LaTeX float placement. `table-top-skip` supplies a TeX length or skip.
